🧳 External / portable drive · 🗑️ Deleted files

Recover Deleted Files From an External Hard Drive

Deleting a file usually just marks its space as free, so the data stays until new files overwrite it. Check the Recycle Bin or Trash first, since many computers keep one on external hard drives too. If the files are not there, recovery tools are your main option.

1/5 · Safe to DIY
Success odds: High

The drive is healthy, so recovery only reads data, as long as you save results to a different drive.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Stop copying, saving or editing files on this drive now. New data can overwrite your deleted files.
  • Do not install recovery software onto the affected drive. Install it on your computer's own drive.
  • Do not save recovered files back to the same drive. Pick a different drive.

Tools you'll use

TestDisk

Free open-source tool that finds lost partitions and repairs boot sectors so files can be read again.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

PhotoRec

Free open-source file carver that recovers files by signature, even when the file system is damaged.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux

🧑‍🔧 When to call a pro

If the drive starts clicking, disconnecting, or the files are irreplaceable and scans find nothing, stop and ask a professional.

Questions people ask

Are deleted files on an external drive in the Recycle Bin?

Often yes. Windows and macOS usually keep a Recycle Bin or Trash on external hard drives, so check there first. If they are not there, stop writing to the drive and use recovery software.

Do I need to take the drive out of its case?

No. Scan it while it is still in the enclosure. Removing it is not needed and can cause problems with some models.

Why are recovered file names missing?

PhotoRec finds files by content, not by their table entry, so names and folders are often lost. TestDisk can sometimes keep them.

Before you start: Educational DIY guide, no warranty. DIY recovery can cause permanent data loss. If the data is valuable, consider a professional first.
